what: Aramark runs the kitchens. It feeds staff and visitors at hospitals, universities, stadiums, prisons and factories under contract, and supplies work uniforms.
customers: Universities, hospitals, sports venues, corporate campuses and correctional facilities, on multi-year contracts.
money: Food and Support Services, United States
campus, healthcare, business and sports catering
the same services in Europe, Latin America and Asia
work uniforms rented, cleaned and delivered
moat: Contracts that run for years and renew at high rates, because changing caterer in a hospital or on a campus means moving staff, kitchens and equipment.
risks: A 1.8% net margin leaves nothing to absorb a shock
Food costs and wages are most of the cost base and both have risen faster than contract prices
$5.7B of debt against $14.5B of market value
opportunities: Analysts see about 22% upside, and revenue grew from $12.1B to $18.5B in four years
New contract wins have outpaced losses, which is what drives growth in this business
Sports and entertainment venues are back to full attendance, the highest-margin part of the mix
watch: Net new business wins and whether food cost inflation is being passed into contract prices.
